what_happened: On a design job, the user corrected Athena's accepted reading 1. The reading would have had the design build the client for the evaluation service (POST /v1/evaluate, several questions per call), a fake for tests and a live test. The repo already has all of these in crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs, and the design doc describes steps 5 and 6 as built. The user restated the reading: reuse the existing client and FakeJev, add only the code-health questions, state builders, thresholds, shadow records and evidence scoring, and cost each landing using batched calls.
cause: The reading step does not survey the code and docs that already exist for the capability before it fixes what the design must build. It works from the request wording and so treats built pieces as new work. Nothing compares the reading's deliverables with the repo's current state, so the overlap surfaced only when the user read the reading. Without that correction, the design would have proposed rebuilding the client, and the verifier would have found it only at the final verdict.
prevention: Add a step before a design reading is accepted. It extracts the named components, endpoints and modules from the reading and searches the snapshot for existing code and doc sections that cover them. For each one it finds, it requires the reading to list it as "reuse" with a file path, or to state why it is replaced. A reading that proposes building something already present fails this check and goes back for revision.
proposed_request: Design the code-health monitoring on top of the existing evaluation client. Before writing the design, read crates/athena-core/src/jev.rs and defaults-loop.md (steps 5 and 6, lines 652-670). Reuse the existing client for POST /v1/evaluate with several questions per call, FakeJev for tests, and the opt-in live test. The design's build plan must list only new work: the code-health questions, their state builders, thresholds, shadow records and evidence scoring. Cost per landing must assume batched calls. Acceptance: (1) the design names the existing jev.rs pieces it reuses and does not propose rebuilding any; (2) the build plan lists only the new items above; (3) the cost per landing figure uses batched calls and shows its arithmetic; (4) the changelog default applies.
